## One picture across the nodes

Port Twin is the design to read when the problem is that every dashboard is a slice. It binds 8 operational systems, 5 live sensor feeds and 1 finance backbone into 13 typed objects and 13 links with the berth as the focal object, joined through three adapter families and one event backbone. The rule a network operator will recognise is the boundary: the twin shows, and pilots, berth planners, engineers and finance staff decide in their own systems, with nothing written back into a system of record. The only model in the register is one self hosted open model, BGE-M3, for document retrieval, about 1.1 GB of fp16 weights on the port's existing enterprise virtual machines, so no equipment is bought. For a logistics network, the transport management system, the warehouse management systems, the telematics feed and the finance system take the places of the port's systems; the pattern of a read only twin over owned systems carries across unchanged, and the object at the centre is the one the network chooses, a shipment, a load or a lane.

## Gate and yard turn time

Terminal Pulse predicts truck turn time two hours out at a container terminal and watches the yard live. The paper's own numbers frame the problem every gate office knows: turn time averages 54 minutes and spikes above 90, and the causes live in separate systems, so planners stitch them together at the morning and afternoon operations meetings and a spike is explained hours after the trucks felt it. The design joins eleven systems, among them the terminal operating system, the gate system, two crane management systems, reefer monitoring, railroad switch lists, cameras and weather and tide feeds, into twelve objects that include the truck visit, the gate lane, the yard block and the transfer zone. Five self hosted open models carry the work: GLM 5.3 for reasoning, Chronos-2 for forecasting, Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B for retrieval, and RF-DETR with Roboflow trackers for vision. Two choices transfer directly to a distribution center's yard or a cross dock gate. The first rollout gate proves or redirects the yard side hypothesis using gate OCR data the operator already holds, before anything else is built. And the surfaces warn and propose while the named planner acts inside the terminal operating system; write back into that system is a second phase option gated on labour and IT sign off. The owned stack is costed at about 722,000 US dollars over three years. The operator in this paper is an illustrative scenario, not a customer.

## Terminal inventory that fails loudly

Loop Integrity Watch answers a question every bulk terminal in a fuel or chemical supply chain shares: is the level reading arriving at the central host continuous, undistorted and attributed to the right tank. The paper names the failure an inventory planner will know, a flatlined gauge reads as a plausible low level and a swapped gauge makes two tanks trade identities, and either one sends a wrong number into every replenishment decision downstream. The design covers 13 fuel tanks on 3 Modbus RTU loops, with 3 booster installations engineered from a measured signal survey inside explosion proof junction boxes, and a governed inventory ontology of 15 typed objects with the fuel tank as the focal object, joined from 2 named source systems through 1 integration adapter family. The model register is empty: every integrity check (stuck value, swap, distortion) is deterministic. The compute is two containers on the operator's own site application server, inside its OT boundary, and every data quality event is acknowledged and resolved by a named person, with the location engineer signing acceptance.

## Fleet faults: the operator's own logic, executed on the vehicle

Consist Watch monitors 225 commuter rail cars, and the part a truck, trailer or locomotive fleet can take is where the logic runs. An onboard module reads 64 named signals per car, 32 digital and 32 analog plus an accelerometer and GPS, and executes the operator's own fault logic table verbatim at the car. Telemetry rides the vehicle's existing cellular routers, a named mechanical desk controller owns every active fault in that territory, and alerts reach named recipient groups by severity. No training run was needed: Chronos-2 handles analog anomaly detection and seasonal trending, and a self hosted open weight reasoning model carries the work surface over the fleet ontology. Centrally it runs on one 141 GB HBM GPU class node in a contractor-hosted US cloud, about 625,000 US dollars for three years on the deepest AWS commitment in US East. A truck maker already publishes the fault codes for its vehicles; this design says where to execute them and who owns the result.

## The control networks at every site, with the evidence

Grid Context Watch is the design for the question an OT security lead and a compliance lead ask together, and a network of terminals, pipelines and automated sites asks it once per site: what is connected to the control networks, whether anything on them is behaving abnormally, and whether that can be proven with evidence when the auditor arrives. It joins 10 source systems, among them the SIEM, an OT detection tool, an IT monitoring platform, the energy management system and the substation data platform, through 2 adapter families into 14 typed objects and 14 links with the OT asset as the focal object, including the vulnerability finding, the detection rule, the pcap evidence record and the CIP evidence artefact. The boundary is read only and one way out of the control networks, and no data leaves the operator. GLM 5.2 (MIT) reasons and Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B (Apache-2.0) retrieves, on one node of eight 141 GB HBM class GPUs; owning that node costs about 510,000 dollars over three years, about four fifths the deepest three-year AWS commitment. Every triage, case and risk acceptance carries a named OT security analyst; agents draft, the analyst decides. The paper's evidence artefacts are written for NERC CIP; a pipeline or terminal operator puts its own security directive in that place, and the shape of control networks watched one way and proven by record carries across.

Sovereign HSE Watch predicts health, safety and environment incidents by joining 8 systems: SAP EHS, PM and QM; SCADA; fire and gas; Vision AI cameras; SQL databases; scanned files; and the identity provider. # Physical AI System Design for Warehousing and Intralogistics: What the Published Designs Already Answer

*No warehousing design has been published in this series yet. Nine of the eighteen open reference architectures already answer the questions a warehouse or distribution center asks first: one picture of the operation from the systems it already runs, dock and yard turn time, people and vehicles seen on camera, fleet and fixed equipment condition, fire and life safety, counting what leaves, and what a records only study can settle before any sensor is bought.*

Structure Phase Watch adds the inbound side: gate movements and delivery windows are objects in its model, read from haulage GPS, gate logs and biometric turnstiles, and every delivery window it drafts is a recommendation recorded with the approver. Its open item of 13 October is the one any camera estate on a loading apron will meet: the paper names dust, glare and heat as what degrades the lenses, and the answer recorded on its page is a cleaning rota plus a confidence drop on a fixed reference target in each camera's view that opens a work order for a named person, with the camera's health held in the object model as a record someone owns.

## People and vehicles on camera

Pit Camera Watch is a fully on premises camera system for a vehicle proving ground: 40 to 60 poles of thermal and visible camera heads, 80 to 120 streams, recorded on an N+1 pair of open source recorders holding 30 days of footage on local disk inside an isolated network. Its human rule is the conservative one a warehouse safety office may want first. Booth operators watch and decide, nothing raises an automated alarm, and only the safety office can export a clip. The one model, D-FINE under Apache-2.0 at about 8 to 124 MB of weights, searches the archive after the fact for a test vehicle, a support vehicle or a pedestrian; it is not in the live safety path. For aisles and docks, the same shape gives an investigation a searchable archive the operator owns without putting a model between a person and a near miss.

Terminal Pulse is the live counterpart. Its model holds a yard person, a transfer zone and a safety event, its detectors and trackers run in fanless enclosures at the yard blocks, gate and quay, no safety reflex crosses a network hop, and the named safety supervisor acknowledges every safety event. A warehouse choosing between the two is choosing whether the cameras search the past or watch the present, and both papers show what each choice costs in hardware and in human workload.

## Fleet faults: the operator's own logic, executed on the vehicle

Consist Watch monitors 225 commuter rail cars, and the part a forklift or tugger fleet can take is where the logic runs. An onboard module reads 64 named signals per car, 32 digital and 32 analog plus an accelerometer and GPS, and executes the operator's own fault logic table verbatim at the car. ## Conveyors and sortation: advise, never trip

Turbine Island Watch reads a rehabilitated steam turbine generator through a one way path from the control system, the vibration monitoring rack and the generator protection systems. Three of its rules transfer to a conveyor drive, a sorter or a stacker crane without change. The read is one way and nothing writes to the control system. The platform advises and the protection layer trips, so every alert carries a prescribed action that a named shift operator acknowledges. And the rollout gate is a number: two false alerts per week, with thresholds tuned only on channels that have provable history. MOMENT-1 detects anomalies zero shot and no training run is needed. The compute is one 48 GB inference card on ruggedised edge servers inside the plant perimeter, costed at about 22,500 US dollars to own over three years.

## Fire and life safety, read only

Factory Fire Watch gives live visibility of fire alarm panels, fire pumps, fire water tanks and energy meters across an operator's highest risk sites, read through panel contacts, PLC inputs and LoRaWAN into an IoT platform hosted in the Kingdom, with never a write path into certified life safety equipment. No server or GPU is bought. The field equipment per site is about 2,600 to 3,200 US dollars in list prices, and a monitoring officer acknowledges or escalates every safety critical alert. The paper's framing suits a high bay building well: a sensor that has stopped reporting still reads as normal, so the design treats silence as a failure to be surfaced. For a distribution center and its sprinkler pumps, the design is the same read only estate with the sites renamed.

## Counting what leaves the building

Steel Count Ledger puts cameras and one sealed GPU industrial PC at every installation point, counts product as it is made, and publishes the counts through a one way link into one record the authority owns. Counting survives a slow wide area link because it happens at the edge, tracker models keep one item from counting twice, and the weighbridge feed serves as acceptance ground truth. Every discrepancy case is judged by a named revenue field officer; the system counts and reconciles and never assesses, and the mill never edits a count. The same pattern counts pallets or cases at an outbound dock door against what the warehouse management system says shipped, with the detector fine tuned per product type and site as the paper describes.

## What the records already prove

Reliability Atlas is the design to read before any sensor is bought. It joins each plant's work orders, trip history and design documents through three read only adapters, as exports rather than live interfaces, into a reliability object model the operator owns. Availability is computed by Monte Carlo simulation on reliability block diagrams built from each plant's own failure study, auditable to ISO 55000, with predictions accepted only by a named reviewer and root cause reports validated only by a named engineer. The model register is empty by design, no hardware is bought, and the study runs on the operator's own in country servers. A warehouse with a maintenance system and years of conveyor and sorter downtime records can run this study first and let it decide which of the designs above it needs second.

## What every one of them keeps constant

Across all nine, four things do not vary. The system runs on hardware the operator controls, or in a cloud or region the operator chose. A named person owns every decision, and nothing executes on equipment. The object model is published as JSON in the hyper-ontology/1 format, so a warehouse can read the exact objects and links before building any of its own. And the cost is computed the same way in every appendix, from the paper's own sizing with every price cited, so the own or rent question has one answer per design rather than a slogan; the comparison across designs is in [Own or Rent the GPUs](https://codeatoms.ai/blog/own-or-rent-the-gpus/).

## What a first warehousing design would have to name

None of the nine holds a storage location, a pick face, an order line, a dock door, a forklift or a pedestrian aisle as an object, and none holds slotting: which item belongs in which location, and why. Terminal Pulse holds a yard block and a container, which is the nearest shape, but no published design reasons over where stock should sit. A first warehousing design adds that object model, and the near miss between a person and a vehicle in an aisle with it. It is the design the [co-build page for warehousing and intralogistics](https://codeatoms.ai/co-build/warehousing-and-intralogistics/) is open for: the operator brings the operation, the systems that already hold its records and one engineer who knows the building; the published designs above are the proof of what comes out.

## Use the designs

Every object model named here is in the paper's package as `ontology/objects.json`, and the same rows are in the [Vertical-Driven Architectures dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/CodeNinjatools/vertical-driven-architectures) and served live by the [codeninja-research MCP server](https://github.com/muhammadumar89/codeninja-research/tree/main/mcp-server), so a coding agent can ask which published design holds a truck visit or a safety event object and read why. Each paper is citable by its DOI on its page. All were reasoned on [CodeNinja Praxis](https://codeatoms.ai/praxis/) and their object models import into [Hyper Ontology](https://codeatoms.ai/hyper-ontology/).

# A Physical AI System Design for a Semiconductor Assembly and Test Line in Pakistan

*The requirement, in the operator's own voice: edge units that read the inspection cameras at every critical station, one governed ontology of the line, named agents that classify and trace while engineers decide, and memory that makes every confirmed outcome improve the next one.*

Canonical: https://codeatoms.ai/blog/physical-ai-system-design-semiconductor-assembly-test-pakistan/
Author: CodeNinja Atoms, Research distribution
Published: 2026-11-09
License: CC BY 4.0
Publisher: CodeNinja Atoms (https://codeatoms.ai), a fully owned subsidiary of CodeNinja
A physical AI system design, for a semiconductor assembly and test line, is one where the system's eyes sit at the stations themselves: edge units beside the bonders, moulders and markers read the inspection cameras as packages pass, classify what they see, and feed one governed model of the line that agents reason over and engineers decide from. This post publishes the requirement we put to [CodeNinja Praxis](https://codeatoms.ai/praxis/) for such a system: a semiconductor assembly and test operator in Pakistan, described by class only, building a new outsourced semiconductor assembly and test (OSAT) line under the national semiconductor roadmap, with its first packaging and test line commissioning in 2026. The published designs of this kind are collected on the [physical AI system design](https://codeatoms.ai/physical-ai-system-design/) page.

## Why an assembly and test line

Wafers arrive diced from fabs abroad. The line attaches die to substrates or lead frames, wire bonds or flip chip bonds them, moulds, marks and singulates the packages, then tests them electrically and inspects them before shipment. The pilot line is sized for a few hundred thousand packages a month in the first year across two or three package families, with a path to tens of millions a year if anchor customers commit.

Back end yield is decided by things that are hard to see and easy to miss: a lifted wire, a cracked die edge, a void under the die attach, a smeared mark, a bent lead. The inspection stations image every package, but they raise far more alerts than a small quality team can review, and a tuned rule that catches one package family misses the next. When an anchor customer rejects a lot, engineers rebuild the story by hand across the bonder log, the mould recipe, the test bin map and the inspection images, which takes days and often ends without a confirmed cause.

This is a new line with a new team. The judgement of the few experienced engineers hired from abroad lives in their heads and leaves with them. A physical AI system is how that judgement becomes a property of the line instead of a property of the people.

## The systems of record

The manufacturing execution system, the equipment data collection on each bonder, moulder and tester, the automated optical inspection stations' own result databases, the test cell's data logs, the quality management system and the customer return log. Every fact the system uses is tied back to one of them.

## What the operator asks for

1. **Physical AI at the station.** Edge units beside the die attach, wire bond, mould and marking stations, on the CodeNinja on device AI stack, that read the inspection cameras as packages pass, classify each defect candidate and keep nothing but the classified result and the evidence frame. The design says which stations get a camera, what each camera looks for and what runs on the unit.
2. **One model of the line.** A governed ontology of lot, substrate, die, package, station, recipe, bonder head, mould tool, inspection run, defect, defect class, test bin, hold, customer return and corrective action, each fact tied to its source system.
3. **Named agents that draft, engineers who decide.** A classification agent, triggered by a new defect candidate, proposes the class with its evidence frame, confirmed by the quality engineer. An excursion agent, triggered by a defect rate crossing its control limit on one station, traces the likely recipe, tool or material lot and drafts a hold, approved by the process engineer. A return agent, triggered by a customer return, assembles the lot's full history and drafts the eight discipline report for the quality manager to approve.
4. **Memory.** Every confirmed class and every traced cause is kept so the next classification and the next trace are better, without training a model on the fly.
5. **A command centre** for the quality and process team with station defect rates, open holds, agent drafts and a conversational interface that answers with citations.
6. **The model named.** Reasoning runs on GLM 5.3 open weights, self hosted on the operator's own servers in Pakistan.

## The rules that bind

- **Inside the plant.** Customer die images, recipes and test data never leave the operator's network. Models are open weights on hardware the operator owns. No third party model service.
- **Rules.** The anchor customers' confidentiality and data protection terms, the export control conditions attached to the equipment and die the line receives, the national data protection rules, and the automotive and consumer quality standards the customers audit against. The design names the approvals it needs.
- **Systems first.** Read from the execution system, the inspection databases and the equipment logs. No agent places or releases a hold without a named approval.
- **People decide.** Agents classify and draft; engineers confirm.

## What success looks like

The first phase covers one package family on one line for one quarter, measured against a baseline of false alert rate, escapes found at final test or by the customer, time from excursion onset to hold, and engineer review hours per lot. The event the design is tested on is one wire bonder drifting and producing lifted wires across three lots, caught at the station, traced and held before the lots reach test.

## What makes it a physical AI system design

Three things separate this from an inspection dashboard.

The intelligence is at the machine. The edge unit beside the bonder classifies the frame while the package is still in reach, so an excursion is caught at the station where it starts, not at final test or at the customer, lots later.

The physical line and the record of it are one model. A lifted wire is not an image in one database and a bin code in another; it is a defect, on a package, from a bonder head, under a recipe, inside a lot, and the agents trace along those relations the way an experienced engineer would.

The outcome feeds back. Every class the quality engineer confirms and every cause the process engineer accepts is written into memory that the next classification and the next trace must read, so the line's judgement compounds with every lot instead of leaving with the engineers who carry it.

## Questions the design must answer

1. Which stations carry cameras, what runs on each edge unit and on the plant servers, and the hardware class, size and three year cost of each, computed from the models' own weights.
2. How the line ontology is built from the operator's systems and kept current lot by lot.
3. How a classification and an excursion trace are explained to an engineer and to a customer auditor.
4. How confirmed outcomes become memory that improves the next result.
5. The first phase's gates for extending to the next package family and the next line.

The published designs that already answer parts of this, vision at the station and plant quality among them, are collected as [physical AI system design](https://codeatoms.ai/physical-ai-system-design/) and as [sovereign AI reference architectures](https://codeatoms.ai/sovereign-ai-reference-architectures/). Every object model is in the [Vertical-Driven Architectures dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/CodeNinjatools/vertical-driven-architectures).

We are reinventing knowledge work to close the loop between vertical AI use cases and the generalized intelligence that fuels it, accelerating the path toward organizational superintelligence.

# A Self-Improving AI System for a Gas Compressor Fleet in Saudi Arabia

*The requirement, in the operator's own voice: one governed ontology of every compression train, named agents that draft and people who decide, and a loop that learns from every closed work order through memory, never by retraining weights.*

Canonical: https://codeatoms.ai/blog/self-improving-ai-system-gas-compressor-fleet-saudi-arabia/
Author: CodeNinja Atoms, Research distribution
Published: 2026-11-02
License: CC BY 4.0
Publisher: CodeNinja Atoms (https://codeatoms.ai), a fully owned subsidiary of CodeNinja
A self-improving AI system, for a gas compressor fleet, is one that gets measurably better at maintenance decisions every time a work order closes, because what was predicted and what was actually found are written back into the context it reasons with, never into retrained weights. This post publishes the requirement we put to [CodeNinja Praxis](https://codeatoms.ai/praxis/) for such a system: a large gas processing operator in Saudi Arabia, described by class only, deciding when to inspect, extend or overhaul its compression trains. The way Praxis itself is run as one is on the [self-improving AI system](https://codeatoms.ai/self-improving-ai-system/) page.

## Why a compressor fleet

Compression is the heart of a gas plant: trains of centrifugal compressors driven by gas turbines and large electric motors run around the clock. Every maintenance decision on a train, inspect now or extend, overhaul or repair, is made by a reliability engineer reading the historian, the vibration system, oil results and old inspection reports by hand.

When the inspection is done, what was found, worse than expected, better, or a different fault, is written into a work order and rarely flows back into the next decision. So the same judgement is relearned train by train, the best engineers' knowledge stays in their heads, and the fleet carries both unnecessary inspections and surprise trips.

An unplanned trip cuts plant throughput and can flare gas. An unnecessary inspection takes a train offline for days. Refurbishment capacity is limited, so every overhaul slot matters. A published 2026 maintenance case study from this class of operator showed that moving from fixed maker intervals to an extend and inspect approach, reading exhaust temperature, compressor discharge, bearing temperature, load, vibration, inlet filter differential pressure and trip logs, extended inspection intervals by 20 to 34 percent on one frame family.

## The systems of record

The plant historian, the vibration and machinery protection system, the maintenance management system, the lube oil laboratory, inspection reports and the makers' service bulletins. Every fact the system uses is tied back to one of them.

## What the operator asks for

1. **A self-improving AI system.** One governed ontology of plant, compression train, compressor, driver, component, sensor tag, reading, trip, inspection, finding, work order, interval decision and service bulletin, each fact tied to its source.
2. **A loop that improves from outcomes.** Every work order outcome, what was predicted and what was found, is written to memory and changes the next recommendation. The system improves loop by loop through memory, never by retraining weights.
3. **Named agents that draft, people who decide.** A condition agent, triggered by a new reading pattern or a trip, ranks each train's risk with its evidence, confirmed by the reliability engineer. An interval agent, triggered by an upcoming scheduled inspection, drafts extend or inspect with the evidence and past outcomes, approved by the maintenance superintendent. An outcome agent, triggered when a work order closes, compares prediction with finding and drafts the lesson into memory, confirmed by the maintenance planner.
4. **Sensing at the edge.** Continuous sensing on the critical trains, route based collection for the rest, at the edge on the CodeNinja on device AI stack.
5. **A command centre** for the reliability team, and a conversational interface whose answers cite their records.
6. **The model named.** Reasoning runs on GLM 5.3 open weights, self hosted in the operator's own data centre in Saudi Arabia.

## The rules that bind

- **Sovereign.** All plant data and models stay in Saudi Arabia on hardware the operator controls. No third party model service. Operational networks stay separated.
- **Rules.** The national cybersecurity controls for operational technology, the Personal Data Protection Law, process safety management, and the operator's own engineering standards and permit to work. The design names the approvals it needs.
- **Read first.** No agent changes a maintenance plan, a protection setting or a work order without a named approval.
- **People decide.**

## What success looks like

The first phase covers one plant's gas turbine driven compressor trains for twelve months, measured against a baseline of unplanned trips, inspections performed versus deferred with no adverse finding, the prediction hit rate on closed work orders, and overhaul slots used. The event the design is tested on is one compressor train tripping on high bearing temperature.

## What makes it self-improving

Three things separate this from a condition monitoring dashboard.

The outcome is recorded against the prediction. When a work order closes, the outcome agent puts the finding next to what the condition and interval agents said before the inspection. That pair is the learning signal.

The lesson changes context, not weights. The confirmed lesson becomes a memory entry that the next recommendation for any similar train must read and cite. Nothing is trained into the model, so every change is a document a reliability engineer can read.

The loop is auditable. Because every lesson is a record with an author, a date and the work order it came from, a bad lesson can be found and retired, and the prediction hit rate on closed work orders shows loop by loop whether the system is actually getting better.

## Questions the design must answer

1. How the fleet ontology is built from the historian and maintenance systems.
2. How each work order outcome changes the next recommendation, measurably, without training a model.
3. What sensing and edge hardware the critical trains need, sized and costed.
4. How the loop is audited so a bad lesson can be found and retired.
5. The first phase's gates for extending to every plant.

The published designs that already answer parts of this, rotating equipment condition monitoring and plant reliability among them, are collected as [physical AI system design](https://codeatoms.ai/physical-ai-system-design/) and as [sovereign AI reference architectures](https://codeatoms.ai/sovereign-ai-reference-architectures/). Every object model is in the [Vertical-Driven Architectures dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/CodeNinjatools/vertical-driven-architectures).

## About CodeNinja

CodeNinja is a Middle Eastern-American artificial intelligence lab focused on building self-improving systems. We are reinventing knowledge work to close the loop between vertical AI use cases and the generalized intelligence that fuels it, accelerating the path toward organizational superintelligence.

# Sensing Comes Before the Model

*Three published earth observation architectures decide what to watch from law, revisit and ownership, never from model accuracy. Two of the three ship with an empty model register.*

Canonical: https://codeatoms.ai/blog/sensing-comes-before-the-model/
Author: CodeNinja Atoms, Research distribution
Published: 2026-10-11
License: CC BY 4.0
Publisher: CodeNinja Atoms (https://codeatoms.ai), a fully owned subsidiary of CodeNinja
The usual way to start an earth observation project is to pick the model. Someone has a segmentation network that works on satellite imagery, and the architecture grows around it.

Three designs in this corpus say the order is wrong. All three are agriculture and earth observation systems, in Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and the United States. In all three the sensing decision is made first and made from constraints that have nothing to do with accuracy: what the law allows, how often the sensor comes back, and who ends up owning the output. In two of the three, no model is committed at all.

## Two of three registers are empty, by decision

[Field Ledger](https://codeatoms.ai/farm-data-dashboard-pakistan/) is an agriculture data dashboard in Pakistan on twelve objects. Its register records zero models, and the reason is written down: the requirement commits aggregations, drill down and reporting, and no model was verified for this run. A forecaster over the sensor time series is named as open work, gated on Milestone 1 evidence rather than assumed into the design.

[Baseline](https://codeatoms.ai/vegetation-mapping-lidar-us/) is a one flight acquisition of 4 band orthoimagery and LiDAR in the United States on sixteen objects. Its register is empty too, for a blunter reason: no model layer was wanted. Vegetation analysis stays with the operator's own staff in the operator's own tools. The entry that follows it is the one most model centric designs never write, that with zero weights there is no model license to hold or to trigger, so ownership runs through the services agreement instead.

[Fodder Watch](https://codeatoms.ai/restricted-crop-monitoring-saudi-arabia/) is the only one of the three that commits models: two, on fourteen objects. A detector, RF-DETR under Apache 2.0, fine tuned per region. A forecaster, Chronos-2 under Apache 2.0, zero shot, about 120M parameters. Both licenses were part of the choice, not a footnote after it.

An empty register is a result, not a gap. It says the cross system join was the hard part and the design did not need a learned component to do it.

## What actually decided the sensing

In each design the sensing entry carries its own reason, and none of the reasons is a benchmark score.

Fodder Watch screens parcels for restricted cultivation. Its optical channel is Sentinel-2 at 10 m with a 5 day revisit, picked because it resolves center pivots for crop class without a foreign processing dependency. Its radar channel is Sentinel-1 C band SAR, and the stated reason is worth reading twice: the cloud proof complement matters because dust and haze, not cloud, are the optical channel's real attacker in that geography. Landsat 8/9 at an 8 day combined revisit is there for the archive reaching back decades, which is what gives each parcel a baseline series. The cloud layer from Sentinel-2 is recorded as evidence in the screening rule rather than as truth.

Baseline flies a manned aircraft with a 4 band red, green, blue and near infrared large format camera, because the requirement excludes unmanned data outright. Its LiDAR is a Quality Level 1 sensor at a minimum 8 pulses per square meter, with the 16 pulse option priced separately and left exercisable. The positioning entry is the one that decides whether the deliverable is QL1 at all: GNSS guidance with network RTK or an owned base station, specified by baselines, correction source and test evidence, because that chain is what the accuracy claim rests on.

Field Ledger installs no sensing whatsoever. It reads the operator's existing sensor devices, read only, no cameras, no new field hardware. The world is sensed by farm rather than watched.

Three systems in one sector, and the sensing ranges from four satellite and aerial sources to none at all. That range is the argument. Sensing is a requirements decision.

## The license is a design constraint, not paperwork

Fodder Watch has an entry that explains itself in one line: RF-DETR XL and 2XL, under Roboflow's Platform Model License, excluded. The reason is that field of use terms would compromise in Kingdom weight ownership.

That is a checkpoint rejected for its license while the smaller checkpoint under Apache 2.0 was kept. If the model had been chosen first and the sovereignty requirement read later, the design would have had to be rebuilt around a constraint it could have honored on day one.

## Where renting is not an option at any price

Fodder Watch needs one 48 GB PCIe card, L40S class, chosen by a footprint rule: the combined weights come to under 0.55 GB, which leaves batch and cache headroom. Owning that node costs about 15,200 dollars over three years, in a range of 14,600 to 15,800 once support at 8 to 12 percent a year and power at a PUE of 1.6 on the Saudi industrial tariff are counted. Renting the same card on demand in the nearest AWS region is about 60,000 dollars over the same three years, and 22,600 dollars on the deepest three year EC2 Instance Savings Plan, all upfront.

Owning wins on money here. But the line that matters in the appendix is the qualifier attached to every rental row: outside the Kingdom. For a service whose whole purpose is that detections stay sovereign, the cheapest cloud number is not a competing option. It is a measurement of what the requirement already ruled out.

## The order the designs actually follow

Read across the three and one order falls out. What the law and the operator permit you to sense. What revisit and resolution that sensing gives you. What objects those readings have to become for the question to be answerable. Only then, whether a learned model is needed at all, and only then, under what license and on whose hardware it runs.

The model is the fourth decision, and twice out of three it turns out not to be a decision at all.

---

*The three designs, their object models as JSON, their model registers and their sourced cost appendices are free to reuse under CC BY 4.0: [Field Ledger](https://codeatoms.ai/farm-data-dashboard-pakistan/), [Baseline](https://codeatoms.ai/vegetation-mapping-lidar-us/), [Fodder Watch](https://codeatoms.ai/restricted-crop-monitoring-saudi-arabia/). All three were designed on [CodeNinja Praxis](https://codeatoms.ai/praxis/) and their object models import into [Hyper Ontology](https://codeatoms.ai/hyper-ontology/). Operations are described by class, never by name.*

# A Sovereign AI Architecture for Refinery Operations Knowledge in Saudi Arabia

*The requirement, in the operator's own voice: one governed ontology of the whole refinery, named agents that draft and shift engineers who decide, open weight models self hosted in country, and memory that makes every trip analysis better than the last.*

Canonical: https://codeatoms.ai/blog/sovereign-ai-architecture-refinery-operations-knowledge-saudi-arabia/
Author: CodeNinja Atoms, Research distribution
Published: 2026-11-09
License: CC BY 4.0
Publisher: CodeNinja Atoms (https://codeatoms.ai), a fully owned subsidiary of CodeNinja
A sovereign AI architecture, for a refinery, is one the operator owns end to end: open weight models running on hardware the operator controls inside Saudi Arabia, reading the refinery's own systems of record, with nothing about the plant leaving the country or reaching a foreign model service. This post publishes the requirement we put to [CodeNinja Praxis](https://codeatoms.ai/praxis/) for such a system: a refining operator in Saudi Arabia, described by class alone, that wants the judgement of its best shift engineers turned into operations knowledge the whole plant can use. The published designs of this kind are collected as [sovereign AI architecture](https://codeatoms.ai/sovereign-ai-architecture/) reference pages.

## Why a refinery

The refinery runs crude distillation, hydrocracking, hydrotreating, reforming, sulphur recovery and utilities around the clock, with a control room per complex and a shift engineer responsible for each. Refineries of this class process several hundred thousand barrels a day, by public reporting on plants of the class in the country, and run a major turnaround every few years with thousands of contractor workers on site.

The shift engineers are asked questions no single system answers. Why did the hydrocracker trip in the same way twice this year. What did the last turnaround find in this exchanger bank. Which procedure change was made after the last sulphur unit upset, and did it work. The answers exist, in the historian, in a shift log, in a change record and in an incident report, and a good engineer spends a night shift joining them.

The urgency is generational. Half the senior shift engineers retire within five years, and the new engineers inherit the systems but not the judgement. During a turnaround the problem doubles: thousands of findings arrive in days, and the engineers who can read them are out on the plant.

## The systems of record

The distributed control system and its historian, the alarm and event journal, the operating procedures and shift logs, the maintenance management system, the management of change records, the incident and near miss system, the laboratory information system and the turnaround planning system. Every fact the system uses is tied back to one of them.

## What the operator asks for

1. **A sovereign AI architecture owned by the operator.** Open weight models on the operator's own hardware in the country, reading the systems of record, with nothing about the plant leaving the country or reaching a foreign model service.
2. **One model of the plant.** A governed ontology of unit, equipment, tag, alarm, procedure, shift log entry, work order, change, incident, lab result, finding and turnaround task, each fact tied to its source system, so an exchanger has one history across the historian, the work orders and the findings.
3. **Named agents that draft, engineers who decide.** A trip analyst, triggered by a unit trip, drafts the sequence of events with the matching earlier trips and the changes made since, confirmed by the shift engineer. A handover agent, triggered by shift end, drafts the handover from the alarms, logs and work orders of the shift for the outgoing engineer to confirm. A findings agent, triggered by a turnaround inspection finding, drafts the matching history and the recommended disposition for the turnaround engineer to approve.
4. **Memory.** Every confirmed cause and every accepted disposition is kept so the next analysis is better, without training a model on the fly.
5. **A command centre** for shift engineers, showing open trips, handovers, findings waiting and agent drafts, with a conversational interface that answers with citations.
6. **The model named.** Reasoning runs on GLM 5.3 open weights, self hosted on the operator's own hardware in Saudi Arabia.

## The rules that bind

- **In country.** Plant data never leaves the operator's network. Models are open weights on hardware the operator owns. No third party model service.
- **Rules.** The national critical infrastructure cybersecurity controls for operational technology, the process safety management rules, the operator's own management of change procedure, and the national data protection law. The design names the approvals it needs.
- **Read only on control systems.** The architecture reads the historian and journals through the existing one way path. It never writes to the control system, and no agent changes a setpoint, a procedure or a work order without a named approval.
- **People decide.** Agents draft; engineers confirm.

## What success looks like

The first phase covers one complex and its control room for one quarter, including the turnaround if it falls in the quarter, measured against a baseline of hours to a confirmed trip sequence, handover completeness, repeat trips with the same cause, and findings dispositioned per day during the turnaround. The simulated event the design is tested on is a hydrocracker recycle compressor trip at night, with the matching trip from last year and the change made after it found and shown to the shift engineer within minutes.

## What makes it a sovereign AI architecture

Three things separate this from a cloud analytics subscription.

The weights live with the plant. Reasoning runs on open weight models on hardware the operator owns inside Saudi Arabia, so the capability cannot be priced up, switched off or routed abroad by a vendor, and nothing about the plant crosses the border to a model service.

The knowledge is the operator's object model, not a vendor's index. The ontology of units, tags, procedures, changes, incidents and findings is governed by the operator and tied fact by fact to the systems of record, so it outlives any one supplier and any one model.

The judgement stays auditable and in country. Every confirmed cause and accepted disposition is a cited record an engineer and a process safety auditor can read, kept as memory on the same sovereign hardware, so the plant's hardest earned knowledge accumulates where it was earned.

## Questions the design must answer

1. What runs where on the operator's hardware, the hardware class and size, and the three year cost computed from the models' own weights.
2. How the plant ontology is built from the systems of record and kept current shift by shift.
3. How a trip sequence and a finding disposition are explained to a shift engineer and to a process safety auditor.
4. How confirmed outcomes become memory that improves the next analysis.
5. The first phase's gates for extending to the other complexes.

The published designs that already answer parts of this, refinery and process plant operations among them, are collected as [physical AI system design](https://codeatoms.ai/physical-ai-system-design/) and as [sovereign AI reference architectures](https://codeatoms.ai/sovereign-ai-reference-architectures/). Every object model is in the [Vertical-Driven Architectures dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/CodeNinjatools/vertical-driven-architectures).

We are reinventing knowledge work to close the loop between vertical AI use cases and the generalized intelligence that fuels it, accelerating the path toward organizational superintelligence.

# A Sovereign AI Reference Architecture for a Container Terminal in Pakistan

*The requirement, in the operator's own voice: one governed ontology of every box from discharge to gate, named agents that draft the chases and the stack moves while planners decide, and open weight models on hardware the operator owns in the country.*

Canonical: https://codeatoms.ai/blog/sovereign-ai-reference-architecture-container-terminal-pakistan/
Author: CodeNinja Atoms, Research distribution
Published: 2026-11-09
License: CC BY 4.0
Publisher: CodeNinja Atoms (https://codeatoms.ai), a fully owned subsidiary of CodeNinja
A sovereign AI reference architecture, for a container terminal, is a complete system design the operator owns end to end: open weight models running on hardware inside the country, reasoning over the terminal's own systems of record, with nothing about customers' cargo leaving the country or reaching a foreign model service. This post publishes the requirement we put to [CodeNinja Praxis](https://codeatoms.ai/praxis/) for such a system: a container terminal operator at a major seaport in Pakistan, described by class only, under pressure from the government's programme to cut container dwell time by two thirds. The architectures that answer requirements like this one are collected on the [sovereign AI reference architectures](https://codeatoms.ai/sovereign-ai-reference-architectures/) page.

## Why a container terminal

A container terminal moves boxes between ships, the yard and the road gate, with the customs authority clearing cargo on the premises and off dock yards taking the overflow. Terminals of this class in Pakistan see container dwell of around a week against a national target of two days, gate queues that stretch into the city, and periodic backlogs of hundreds of boxes that make the news. Trucks now need tracking devices fitted before they can carry cargo out, which has added hours to gate turnaround.

Every box that overstays has a reason, and the operator learns it late: a release the shipping line has not sent, a customs hold nobody chased, a consignee who has not booked a truck, a yard stack that buries the box under newer arrivals. The gate backs up when the yard cannot deliver boxes in appointment order, and the yard cannot plan when it does not know which boxes will clear today.

The planners know the lines, the agents and the cargo types that overstay most. None of that knowledge is written anywhere, so each planner starts the shift from a fresh list. And when the trade bodies or the port authority ask why a box took nine days to leave, the answer is assembled from four systems by hand.

## The systems of record

There are seven: the terminal operating system, the gate operating system and its cameras, the customs authority's clearance messages, the shipping lines' manifests and releases, the yard equipment telematics, the truck appointment system and the off dock transfer log. Every fact the system uses is tied back to one of them.

## What the operator asks for

1. **A sovereign AI reference architecture.** Open weight models on hardware the operator owns in Pakistan, reading the terminal's systems and the customs authority's messages, with nothing about customers' cargo leaving the country or reaching a foreign model service.
2. **One model of the operation.** A governed ontology of vessel call, container, consignee, agent, line, release, customs state, hold, yard position, stack, appointment, truck, gate transaction, dwell and off dock transfer, each fact tied to its source system, so one box has one story from discharge to gate.
3. **Named agents that draft, planners who decide.** An overstay agent, triggered by a box passing half its free time without a clearance step, drafts the chase to the line, the agent or the authority and the recommended off dock transfer, approved by the yard planner. A stack agent, triggered by the next day's clearances, drafts the housekeeping moves that put tomorrow's deliveries on top, approved by the yard superintendent. A gate agent, triggered by an appointment queue crossing its threshold, drafts the lane and slot changes for the gate supervisor to approve.
4. **Memory.** Every confirmed overstay cause and every accepted housekeeping plan is kept, so the next plan is better, without training a model on the fly.
5. **A command centre** for the planning team, with boxes ranked by dwell and cause, chases open, housekeeping drafts, gate queue state, agent drafts awaiting approval, and a conversational interface that answers with citations.
6. **The model named.** Reasoning runs on GLM 5.3 open weights, self hosted on the operator's own hardware in Pakistan.

## The rules that bind

- **In country.** Cargo, customer and gate camera data never leave the operator's network. Models are open weights on hardware the operator owns. No third party model service.
- **Rules.** The port authority's concession terms, the customs authority's clearance rules and message formats, the national data protection rules for gate cameras and drivers, and the shipping lines' data terms. The design names the approvals it needs.
- **Systems first.** The system reads from the terminal, gate and customs systems. No agent moves a box, releases a hold or changes an appointment without a named approval.
- **People decide.** Agents watch and draft; planners and supervisors confirm.

## What success looks like

Phase one covers import containers on one yard block and one gate complex for one quarter, measured against a baseline of median dwell days, boxes over seven days, housekeeping moves per delivered box and gate turnaround minutes. The event the design is tested on is a shipping line's release file arriving late for forty boxes due out tomorrow: seen, chased, and the stack replanned overnight so the morning appointments still clear.

## What makes it a sovereign reference architecture

Three things separate this from a terminal analytics product bought off the shelf.

The data never leaves. Cargo manifests name customers and their goods, and gate cameras record trucks and drivers. All of it stays on the operator's network in Pakistan, and the models that reason over it are open weights on hardware the operator owns, never a third party model service that another jurisdiction can switch off or read.

The design is owned, not rented. The architecture must say what runs where on the operator's hardware, the hardware class and size, and the three year cost, so the operator can buy, run and replace every part of it. That is what makes it a reference: another terminal in the country facing the same dwell targets can take the same design.

The authority can audit it. Because every fact in the ontology is tied to its source system, an overstay chase or a housekeeping plan can be explained line by line to a planner, to the port authority and to the trade bodies asking why a box took nine days.

## Questions the design must answer

1. What runs where on the operator's hardware, the hardware class and size, and the three year cost computed from the models' own weights.
2. How the terminal ontology is built from the operator's systems and the authority's messages, and kept current move by move.
3. How an overstay chase and a housekeeping plan are explained to a planner and to the port authority.
4. How confirmed outcomes become memory that improves the next plan.
5. Phase one's gates for extending to export containers and the other yard blocks.

The published designs this requirement sits beside are collected as [physical AI system design](https://codeatoms.ai/physical-ai-system-design/) and as [sovereign AI reference architectures](https://codeatoms.ai/sovereign-ai-reference-architectures/). Every object model is in the [Vertical-Driven Architectures dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/CodeNinjatools/vertical-driven-architectures).

## About CodeNinja

CodeNinja is a Middle Eastern-American artificial intelligence lab focused on building self-improving systems. We are reinventing knowledge work to close the loop between vertical AI use cases and the generalized intelligence that fuels it, accelerating the path toward organizational superintelligence.

# The Model Register Across Sixteen Designs

*Sixteen open reference architectures for physical operations, each with a model register the operator owns outright. Twelve models, four empty registers by decision, and one licence pattern that repeats in every design.*

Canonical: https://codeatoms.ai/blog/the-model-register-across-sixteen-designs/
Author: CodeNinja Atoms, Research distribution
Published: 2026-10-13
License: CC BY 4.0
Publisher: CodeNinja Atoms (https://codeatoms.ai), a fully owned subsidiary of CodeNinja
A model register is the part of a system design that names every learned component the operation will run, with its licence, its size and the reason it was chosen over the alternatives. Sixteen open reference architectures on this site carry one, and every row of every register is in the public dataset as `models.jsonl`. This note lines them up.

Two things stand out before the table. Four of the sixteen designs have an empty register, and in each case the emptiness is a decision the paper defends rather than a gap. And no design holds a model under a licence with a field of use restriction, a revenue trigger or a copyleft clause that would reach the operator's own code. Weight ownership is the rule the whole corpus runs on.

## The reasoning models

Five designs put a frontier class open weight model behind a work surface for the operation's own people and agents. All five chose a GLM model from the same family, self hosted at FP8 on one node of eight 141 GB HBM class GPUs, and the register says why in licence terms.

| Model | Licence | Designs that chose it | The reason the register gives |
|---|---|---|---|
| GLM 5.3, 753B mixture of experts, FP8 | Bespoke licence permitting internal commercial use with attribution and no revenue trigger | [Sovereign HSE Watch](https://codeatoms.ai/sovereign-hse-pakistan/), [Steel Count Ledger](https://codeatoms.ai/steel-production-count-pakistan/), [Terminal Pulse](https://codeatoms.ai/truck-turn-container-terminal-us/) | Strongest open agentic model; purely internal use is exempt from the model as a service security review trigger; 904 GB of weights against one node of 1,128 GB leaves KV headroom |
| GLM 5.2, 753B, FP8, 1M context | MIT | [Grid Context Watch](https://codeatoms.ai/ot-security-cip-evidence-us/), [Feeder Firewatch](https://codeatoms.ai/wildfire-risk-distribution-us/) | A plain MIT licence with no revenue trigger or security review clause; one node holds it |

The split is not an accident. Where the operator wanted the strongest agentic behaviour, the design accepted a bespoke licence whose internal use carve out it had read. Where the operator was a utility or a cooperative with an auditor behind it, the design took the one generation older model under MIT and gave up nothing it needed.

## The detectors and trackers

Among the designs that watch with cameras, five chose the same detector.

| Model | Licence | Designs that chose it | The reason the register gives |
|---|---|---|---|
| RF-DETR, Nano to Large checkpoints, BF16, about 61 to 68 MB at 16 bit | Apache 2.0 | [Sovereign HSE Watch](https://codeatoms.ai/sovereign-hse-pakistan/), [Steel Count Ledger](https://codeatoms.ai/steel-production-count-pakistan/), [Feeder Firewatch](https://codeatoms.ai/wildfire-risk-distribution-us/), [Terminal Pulse](https://codeatoms.ai/truck-turn-container-terminal-us/), [Fodder Watch](https://codeatoms.ai/restricted-crop-monitoring-saudi-arabia/) | The practical sovereign answer to the AGPL gate; fine tuned on the operator's own footage; the operator owns and hardens the weights. Two designs exclude the XL and 2XL checkpoints because they sit under a platform licence whose field of use terms would compromise weight ownership |
| D-FINE, N to X tiers, BF16 | Apache 2.0 | [Pit Camera Watch](https://codeatoms.ai/test-site-camera-monitoring-us/) | An unconditional licence; the N through L tiers fit one 48 GB card; ahead of DEIM on matched compute |
| Roboflow trackers, ByteTrack and OC-SORT class | Apache 2.0 | [Sovereign HSE Watch](https://codeatoms.ai/sovereign-hse-pakistan/), [Structure Phase Watch](https://codeatoms.ai/structure-phase-construction-saudi-arabia/), [Steel Count Ledger](https://codeatoms.ai/steel-production-count-pakistan/) | Stable identity across frames without reintroducing copyleft after an Apache detector; one billet crossing two camera fields counts once |
| Anomalib 2.7.0, FP32, exported to ONNX Runtime | Apache 2.0 | [Hangar Form Cell](https://codeatoms.ai/dieless-sheet-metal-cell-aerospace-mro-us/) | Unsupervised fit on the facility's own good panels needs no labelled defect set |

The pattern a developer should copy is the pairing: an Apache detector followed by an Apache tracker. The register in three designs says in so many words that the tracker was chosen so that the AGPL exposure of the better known tracking collections never enters the serving path.

## The forecasters

| Model | Licence | Designs that chose it | The reason the register gives |
|---|---|---|---|
| Chronos-2, about 120M parameters, about 0.48 GB at FP32 | Apache 2.0 | [Sovereign HSE Watch](https://codeatoms.ai/sovereign-hse-pakistan/), [Terminal Pulse](https://codeatoms.ai/truck-turn-container-terminal-us/), [Fodder Watch](https://codeatoms.ai/restricted-crop-monitoring-saudi-arabia/) | Zero shot multivariate forecasting with covariates and no field of use restriction; thousands of independent per parcel series with no fine tuning dependency |
| Chronos-Bolt | Apache 2.0 | [Hangar Form Cell](https://codeatoms.ai/dieless-sheet-metal-cell-aerospace-mro-us/) | Learns per arm, per stylus load baselines on the edge box and flags drifting pass signatures |
| IBM Granite Tiny Time Mixers TTM-R2, about 0.85M parameters, FP32, about 0.003 GB | Apache 2.0 | [Factory Fire Watch](https://codeatoms.ai/factory-fire-monitoring-saudi-arabia/) | A CPU only forecaster inside the operator's existing platform; the requirement asked for no server or GPU, so none was deployed |

The Granite row is the one to notice. The design covers a hundred factories and runs its forecaster on the CPU the operator already has, because a model of under a million parameters was enough and the requirement forbade buying compute.

## Retrieval and document parsing

| Model | Licence | Designs that chose it | The reason the register gives |
|---|---|---|---|
| BGE-M3, 568M parameters, FP16 | MIT | [Sovereign HSE Watch](https://codeatoms.ai/sovereign-hse-pakistan/), [Port Twin](https://codeatoms.ai/port-digital-twin-us/), [Structure Phase Watch](https://codeatoms.ai/structure-phase-construction-saudi-arabia/) | Dense plus sparse plus multi vector retrieval in one pass with an 8,192 token window; multilingual retrieval across a workforce tagged by language; in the port design it is the only model in the register |
| Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B, 32K window, about 1.2 GB at BF16 | Apache 2.0 | [Grid Context Watch](https://codeatoms.ai/ot-security-cip-evidence-us/), [Terminal Pulse](https://codeatoms.ai/truck-turn-container-terminal-us/) | Whole playbooks, CIP procedures or a whole shift's gate record retrieve as single passages; runs beside the frontier model |
| PaddleOCR-VL 1.6, about 0.9B parameters, BF16 | Apache 2.0 | [Sovereign HSE Watch](https://codeatoms.ai/sovereign-hse-pakistan/), [Corridor Guard](https://codeatoms.ai/dc-interference-gas-pipelines-pakistan/) | Strong on degraded multilingual scans; no user or revenue threshold; digitises a scanned package with human reconciliation before any value enters the record |

The choice between the two embedders is a window question. BGE-M3 wins where the corpus is drawings, inspections and messages in several languages. Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B wins where a single document, a procedure or a shift log, must retrieve whole, and its 32K window makes that possible.

## The four empty registers

| Design | What the register says | Why |
|---|---|---|
| [Reliability Atlas](https://codeatoms.ai/plant-reliability-assessment-saudi-arabia/) | None: the register is empty by design | No inference workload is contracted; the deliverable is the study, and an empty register recorded plainly outranks a speculative entry |
| [Loop Integrity Watch](https://codeatoms.ai/tank-gauge-integrity-pakistan/) | Zero entries; all integrity logic is deterministic thresholds and rules | The failure modes are physical and protocol level, so no learned model is needed, no weights are held and no licence question arises |
| [Field Ledger](https://codeatoms.ai/farm-data-dashboard-pakistan/) | Zero models committed; a forecaster over sensor time series stays open work gated on the first milestone's evidence | The requirement commits aggregations, drill down and reporting, and no model was verified for this run |
| [Baseline](https://codeatoms.ai/vegetation-mapping-lidar-us/) | None; the register is empty by decision | No agent or model layer was wanted; analysis stays with the operator's own staff in their own tools |

A quarter of the designs needed no learned model at all. Each of those papers still carries the register, with its emptiness and the reason written down, because a reader deciding whether to copy the design needs to know that the absence was chosen.

## The licence pattern

Across the twelve named models the licences are Apache 2.0 (nine models), MIT (two) and one bespoke licence read for its internal use carve out. Three things never appear: a field of use restriction on a model the operator fine tunes, a revenue or user threshold, and a copyleft licence in the serving path. Where a stronger checkpoint existed under a platform licence, the register excludes it by name and says why.

That is the whole method. Choose the model for the job, read the licence as carefully as the benchmark, and write the reason down where the next engineer will find it.

## Use the register

The rows behind this note are the `models.jsonl` file of the [Vertical-Driven Architectures dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/CodeNinjatools/vertical-driven-architectures), one row per choice with the design, the choice, what was picked and why. The same file is served live by the [codeninja-research MCP server](https://github.com/muhammadumar89/codeninja-research/tree/main/mcp-server), so a coding agent can ask which designs chose a given model and read the reason. Every design named above was reasoned on [CodeNinja Praxis](https://codeatoms.ai/praxis/) and its object model imports into [Hyper Ontology](https://codeatoms.ai/hyper-ontology/).

# What Does It Take to Vibe Code a Truck?

*Software can now be described into existence. Physical systems cannot, because the knowledge needed to design them lives in the heads of senior engineers. This is how CodeNinja Atoms is building the missing piece: deep domain expertise for physical AI system design, carried as context instead of trained into weights.*

Canonical: https://codeatoms.ai/blog/what-does-it-take-to-vibe-code-a-truck/
Author: Muhammad Umar, Cofounder, CodeNinja
Published: 2026-10-18
License: CC BY 4.0
Publisher: CodeNinja Atoms (https://codeatoms.ai), a fully owned subsidiary of CodeNinja
A year ago, vibe coding meant something new. You describe the app you want, a model writes it, you run it, you describe what is wrong, and it fixes it. A person with no training in software can now ship working software.

So here is the question I keep coming back to. What would it take to vibe code a truck?

Not the cab or the paint. The whole system. An autonomous haul truck working in a copper mine, the fleet it belongs to, the network it talks over, the people who work around it, and the regulator who has to sign it off.

Today no model can do that. This post is about why, and about what we are building at CodeNinja Atoms to change it.

## The Truck

Start with what an engineer actually has to decide before an autonomous haul truck moves a single tonne.

**Sensing.** Which lidar, radar and cameras, where they sit, and what they can see in dust, rain and at night. A sensor that works on a highway can fail on a haul road.

**Compute.** What runs on the truck, what runs at the edge of the pit, and what runs in a data center. How much power, cooling and memory each one needs, and what happens when the link drops.

**Models.** Which perception, prediction and planning models, at what size, trained or adapted on what data, and how each one is monitored once it is running.

**The site.** Haul roads, loading points, crushers, fuel bays, light vehicles driven by people, and the private network that ties them together. The truck is only safe if the site is designed around it.

**Safety and approvals.** Autonomous mining machines have their own safety standards, and each country adds its own rules on top. Someone has to write the safety case, and someone has to approve it.

**Cost and time.** What the system costs over three years, what it saves, and how long it takes before the first truck runs on its own.

**Maintenance.** How the fleet knows a part is about to fail, and who acts on it.

Every one of these decisions depends on the others. Change the sensor and the compute changes. Change the country and the approval path changes. That web of decisions is system design, and for physical AI it is one of the hardest problems there is.

## The Bottleneck

A model can write software because it has read more software than any person ever will. Billions of lines of code are public, along with the questions people asked about them and the answers that worked.

Physical system design is not like that. The knowledge sits in tender documents, internal standards, site reports and, above all, in the heads of engineers who spent twenty years in mining, oil and gas, ports or power. Very little of it is written down, and almost none of it is public.

So the bottleneck in physical AI is not the model. It is deep domain expertise. A young engineer can learn to code in a year. Learning to design a mine takes a career.

That is the problem we set out to solve. Our mission is to let a young engineer design the physical AI systems that whole industries run on, without first spending twenty years in those industries.

## CodeNinja Atoms

CodeNinja Atoms is how we work on that mission in the open. It has four parts.

**Praxis** is the platform. An engineer brings a requirement, often a real tender, and Praxis reasons out the full system design: sensing, compute, models, the object model of the operation, cost, timeline and the approvals it will need. It explains every choice, so the engineer learns the design instead of just receiving it. Praxis is free for engineers.

**Hyper Ontology** is the shared language of those designs. Every design carries an object model of the operation, the assets, people, events and rules, and how they connect, in an open JSON format called hyper-ontology/1.

**The reference architectures** are the designs we publish. There are eighteen so far, across energy, oil and gas, ports, manufacturing, agriculture, rail and more, in the United States, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan. Together their object models hold 246 typed objects and 228 links. They are on [codeatoms.ai](https://codeatoms.ai/sovereign-ai-reference-architectures/) and as a dataset on [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/datasets/CodeNinjatools/vertical-driven-architectures).

**PADI**, the Physical AI Design Index, is the benchmark. It asks a simple question: does the Praxis platform design better systems than frontier AI on its own? It scores both on fresh tasks across 13 industries in three countries. In our latest round, a blind evaluation on seven tasks the platform had never seen, the Praxis platform passed 48.5% of the checks against 28.4% for frontier AI, and came out ahead on all seven tasks. The results are on the [PADI page](https://codeatoms.ai/padi/).

## Compression and Reinflation

The obvious way to give a model domain expertise is to fine tune it. Collect the data, train the weights, ship the model.

We chose not to, and I wrote about why in a memo, [Compression and Reinflation](https://codeatoms.ai/memos/compression-and-reinflation/). Here is the short version.

Fine tuning freezes what you know into weights. The day training ends, the world has already moved: a new regulation, a new site, a new country. And when a better model arrives, the money spent on the old weights is gone.

So we keep expertise as context instead. It works in two steps.

**Compression.** Every day, routines run over what the platform has learned: from real deals, from benchmark rounds, and from engineers correcting a design. Many observations become one sharp principle. Contradictions are resolved. What proved itself rises and what never mattered fades. What is left is small. It is not a record of everything that happened. It is the meaning of what happened.

**Reinflation.** When a new requirement arrives, say a copper mine in a country we have never worked in, no stored principle fits it exactly. It was never meant to. The model reads the compressed expertise and expands it into this site, this country's rules, this fleet and these people. The same lesson becomes a different design every time, because the world it lands in is different every time.

The idea comes from biology. The biologist Michael Levin describes memory as a bowtie: a lot of experience squeezed through a narrow middle and then expanded again for a new body and a new world. A caterpillar's lessons survive inside the butterfly, remapped for wings instead of legs.

There is one rule that makes this work. Everything is context for the model to reason over. Never a keyword match, never a lookup.

## Why It Beats Fine Tuning

Keeping expertise as context instead of weights changes four things.

**It stays current.** A new regulation is one new entry, not a new training run.

**It stays readable.** An engineer can see what the system knows, where it came from, and correct it. Nobody can read a weight.

**It survives the model.** When a stronger open weights model arrives, the expertise carries straight over and the designs improve on day one.

**It stays with the owner.** The expertise lives inside the customer's own perimeter, on their own infrastructure. For a sovereign deployment, that is the whole point.

## Back to the Truck

So what would it take to vibe code a truck?

An engineer would describe the operation: an autonomous haul fleet for a copper mine, in a named country, with a target output and a budget. The system would come back with the sensing, the compute, the models, the site network, the object model of the mine, the safety case outline, the approvals, the three year cost and the plan. Then the engineer would push back, as engineers do, and the system would explain itself and change.

That is not science fiction, and it is not finished either. It needs a model that is good at reasoning, which we now have. It needs deep domain expertise, carried in a form the model can read and an engineer can check, which is what we are building. And it needs a way to measure whether the designs are any good, which is why PADI exists.

When those three come together, the most complex physical systems in the world stop being the work of a handful of people with twenty years behind them. A young engineer anywhere can design them, and understand every choice they made.

Explore the designs, the benchmark and the platform at [codeatoms.ai](https://codeatoms.ai).

At a glance

## A Self-Improving AI System for Canal Irrigation Water Allocation in Pakistan

**What this is.** An open reference architecture for a self-improving AI system in physical AI, built for a provincial irrigation department in Pakistan that takes its share of river water at barrages and head regulators and delivers it through a main canal, distributaries and minors to outlets farmers share by rotation, where owning the inference hardware that runs it costs about 636,000 US dollars over three years. When a head regulator reading drops below its indent for three days at peak demand, the design joins the telemetry, the indent and release ledgers, the rotation schedule, the gauge reader's diary, the complaint register and the revenue crop records into one entitlement versus delivery argument, so the divisional engineer sees which reach is silted, which branch is over drawing and which gate adjustment cured the matching shortfall last season. Every model runs on the department's own hardware inside Pakistan under the inter provincial water accord, canal and drainage law, the national data rules for farmer records and export control on the GPU node. It is written for the officer accountable for canal water allocation, the divisional and subdivisional engineers who set indents and gates, and the data, ontology and platform engineers who would build and run it. The operator is described by class, never by name.

**The answer in numbers.**

| Part | The design |
| --- | --- |
| Sources | Eight read only systems of record, entering through two adapter families (a telemetry adapter doing a direct historian read, and an integration adapter running an OCR pipeline with a human verification stage and a 2 percent failure gate on every batch) that stamp every item with its source, adapter, timestamp and verification state: the telemetry system, the barrage and head regulator gauge records, the indent and release ledgers, the rotation schedules per distributary, the gauge reader diaries, the complaint register and the revenue crop records among them; the platform never operates a gate and never writes into a system of record |
| Object model | 16 typed objects with 13 typed links, from the barrage, head regulator, main canal, distributary, reach, gate and outlet through the rotation, shortfall and season to the indent, release, complaint and crop area, with the telemetry reading and gauge reading as measures, built as a projection over the systems of record and published as JSON for reuse |
| Models | Frontier class open weights for the three drafting agents (shortfall, indent and dispute) and the command centre, self hosted for sovereignty; the operator names GLM 5.3 and the plan holds its FP8 arithmetic, but no weights are committed until the register verifies a model live; embedding, OCR and forecasting model classes for retrieval, handwritten Urdu and English ledgers and shortfall detection; no third party model service, nothing trained into weights |
| Compute | One node of eight 141 GB HBM cards (about 1,128 GB) in the department's circle server room, the held arithmetic for about 756 GB of FP8 weights, beside a 48 GB PCIe class site server for the small model tier; no edge tier, nothing served at a canal head. The node sits above the US advanced computing export threshold for a D:2, D:3 and D:4 destination, so the export licence determination runs first in phase one with an in country procurement route or colocation fallback named before any order |
| Rollout | Two phases carrying 17 scope items (16 and 1), each closed by a gate, never a date: a main canal prototype whose gate is the governed canal network ontology reconciled against one real week of telemetry and ledgers before any agent drafts, one main canal and its distributaries live for one cropping season, then extension to the other canals; baselines reconciled in the first month, headline measure the percent of tail outlets receiving their rotation share, nominal 85 percent, with days from shortfall onset to correction and complaints per distributary beside it |

Renting is a price reference only, because AWS lists no region in Pakistan and every rented option would carry telemetry and ledgers across the border; the frontier footprint itself stands only when the register verifies a model (Appendix A) |

ABSTRACT

## A Shortfall Should Surface Within the Rotation, Not After the Complaint

A provincial irrigation department in Pakistan needs one question answered continuously, and the self-improving AI system it asked for exists to answer it: did every distributary on the main canal receive its entitlement share this rotation, and if not, where, why and what should be done about it. It cannot answer the question today because the answer lives in pieces no system joins: telemetry measures what arrived at the main heads within minutes, the indent and release ledgers state what was asked for and released, the gauge reader diaries record what the field saw, and the complaint register is the first signal that a tail has gone short, usually after the crop is lost. This is the problem ontologies for canal water allocation exist to solve, and in the Indus basin it is politically sensitive, because inter provincial water is contested and the same shortfalls recur every season at the same tails.

The design is a sovereign, self-improving allocation system for one main canal in its first season: eight source systems, two adapter families, a governed ontology of sixteen objects with typed links, six services, three surfaces and three drafting agents for shortfall, indent and dispute, each confirmed by a named engineer. Telemetry enters through a historian read and every paper source through an OCR pipeline with a human verification stage; together they feed one object model that is a projection over the systems of record, never a replacement of them. Improvement runs through memory rather than training: confirmed causes and accepted adjustments compound season over season, so the tails get their share more often without any model being trained on the fly. Everything runs on the operator's own hardware inside Pakistan, in the circle server room, with frontier-class open weights self-hosted for sovereignty; the model register stands open, with no weights committed until a model is verified live, and nothing about the canals leaves the country.

The paper covers the industry problem and the join failure across the existing systems, the constraints and scoping decisions, the stack, the object model, ingestion, inference placement, the open model register, the rollout in two phases carrying seventeen items with their gates and measurements, and ownership of what the system builds. It closes with the chapter that shows how Praxis, the platform the design was produced on, contextualized and reasoned it.
